blocks.text: VPN (for Legacy Apps) enables support for legacy applications that require server-to-client traffic using real IP address binding (e.g., VoIP or Active FTP). This service uses VPN Service Edges, Network Connectors, Network segments, and Zscaler Client Connector. The Network Connector is deployed within your application server's data center, and connects to all known VPN Service Edges. Organizations must configure the route to the client IP pool using the Network Connector's IP address as the next hop.

VPN (for Legacy Apps) connections are only established if each entity (Network Connectors, VPN Service Edges, and Zscaler Client Connector) has the public and private key pairs of the other entities. You can configure a single Network Connector per Network Connector group.
Network Connectors provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Build a secure a tunnel to the VPN (for Legacy Apps) gateway.
Connect applications as part of a Network Connector group to the VPN Service Edge.
Deploy Network Connectors in your tenant using OAuth 2.0 enrollment tokens or provisioning keys.

blocks.text: Private Access (ZPA) supports Windows and macOS platforms for VPN (for Legacy Apps). Network Connectors can only be deployed with RHEL9 in the RPM format for Linux.
On the Network Connectors page (Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > Network Connectors), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Hide the filters on the page by clicking Hide Filters. Click Show Filters to show the filters.
Refresh the Network Connectors page to reflect the most current information.

Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Add a Network Connector.
View a list of all deployed Network Connectors. Network Connectors that you've added, but have not deployed, are not listed. For each deployed Network Connector, you can see:
Name: The name of the Network Connector. OAuth-enabled Network Connectors are added with a name format of GroupName-UserCode-TimeStamp. Click the name to view the details for the Network Connector.
View details for each deployed Network Connector.
Description: The description of the Network Connector, if available.
Network Connector Group: The Network Connector group that the Network Connector is a member of.
Enrollment Certificate: The certificate the Network Connector uses for enrollment. You can click the Edit icon to edit the properties of the certificate.
Host Platform: The platform that the Network Connector is deployed on (e.g., Linux).
Host OS: The run time OS on which the Network Connector is running (e.g., Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9).
Package OS: The compile time OS on which the RPM binary is packaged (e.g., Linux).
Last Software Update: The date and time the Network Connector was last updated to a newer software version.
Last Manager Update: The date and time the Manager software was last updated to a later software version.
Last OS Update: The date and time the OS was last updated to a later software version.
Public Service Edge: The Public Service Edge for Private Access that the Network Connector connects to.
Last Connection to Zscaler: The last time the Network Connector connected to Zscaler.
Last Disconnect from Zscaler: The last time the Network Connector disconnected from Zscaler.
Location: The location where the Network Connector group that the Network Connector belongs to is set up.
Public IP: The public IP address of the Network Connector. Disconnected Network Connectors show the last known public IP address.
Private IP: The private IP address of the Network Connector. Disconnected Network Connectors show the last known private IP address.
Uptime: The period of time the Network Connector is available for use. Disconnected Network Connectors are shown as Not Available.
Enrollment Time: The date and time the Network Connector was enrolled.
Operating System Updates: Indicates whether automatic updates for the OS are enabled or disabled.

Automated OS security updates are only available for prebuilt Network Connector images on RHEL 9.x. Network Connectors installed manually using an RPM file on a custom RHEL 9.x build are not supported.
Connection Health: The health of the Network Connector connection (Connected or Disconnected).
Secure Shell (SSH): Indicates whether the default OS SSH setting is overridden and enabled or disabled.
Manager Version: The current Network Connector Manager software version.
Software Version: The current Network Connector software version.
Version Profile: The version profile applied to the Network Connector.

Hover over the Information icon next to the version profile column heading to view a description of it. If a custom version profile is configured, hover over the Custom link in the table to view its details.
Connection Status: The status of the Network Connector connection.
Upgrade Status: The status of the Network Connector software update.
Status: Indicates whether the Network Connector is enabled or disabled.
Manager Update: The status of the Network Connector update.
Hover over the Information icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the scheduled version and upgrade window.
OS Update: The status of the OS update.
Hover over the Information icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the update window and status of the update (Scheduled, Not Scheduled, In Progress, Success, or Failure).
Edit the configuration of a deployed Network Connector.
Delete a deployed Network Connector configuration.
